content: The monitoring of the health workforce is essential and should be tailored to align with national priorities. Below is a detailed breakdown of health-related occupations, categorized according to the International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-08): 1. Health Professionals (Group Code 22): Medical Doctors (221): Generalist Medical Practitioners (2211) Specialist Medical Practitioners (2212) Nursing and Midwifery Professionals (222): Nursing Professionals (2221) Midwifery Professionals (2222) Traditional and Complementary Medicine Professionals (223): Traditional and Complementary Medicine Professionals (2230) Paramedical Practitioners (224): Paramedical Practitioners (2240) Other Health Professionals (226): Dentists (2261) Pharmacists (2262) Environmental and Occupational Health and Hygiene Professionals (2263) Physiotherapists (2264) Dieticians and Nutritionists (2265) Audiologists and Speech Therapists (2266) Optometrists and Ophthalmic Opticians (2267) Health Professionals Not Elsewhere Classified (2269) 2. Health Associate Professionals (Group Code 32): Medical and Pharmaceutical Technicians (321): Medical Imaging and Therapeutic Equipment Technicians (3211) Medical and Pathology Laboratory Technicians (3212) Pharmaceutical Technicians and Assistants (3213) Medical and Dental Prosthetic and Related Technicians (3214) Nursing and Midwifery Associate Professionals (322): Nursing Associate Professionals (3221) Midwifery Associate Professionals (3222) Traditional and Complementary Medicine Associate Professionals (323): Traditional and Complementary Medicine Associate Professionals (3230) Other Health Associate Professionals (325): Dental Assistants and Therapists (3251) Medical Records and Health Information Technicians (3252) Community Health Workers (3253) Dispensing Opticians (3254) Physiotherapy Technicians and Assistants (3255) Medical Assistants (3256) Environmental and Occupational Health Inspectors and Associates (3257) Ambulance Workers (3258) Health Associate Professionals Not Elsewhere Classified (3259) 3. Personal Care Workers in Health Services (Group Code 532): Health Care Assistants (5321) Home-Based Personal Care Workers (5322) Personal Care Workers in Health Services Not Elsewhere Classified (5329) 4. Additional Health-Related Unit Groups: Health Service Managers (1342) Aged Care Service Managers (1343) Psychologists (2634) Social Work and Counseling Professionals (2635) Social Work Associate Professionals (3412) Medical Secretaries (3344) Biomedical Engineers (2149) Accreditation and Standards in Health Workforce Education: Accreditation is a formal process conducted by an authorized body to assess and certify the quality of educational institutions or programs. This process evaluates learning outcomes, competencies, and adherence to established standards. Accreditation mechanisms include procedures for implementation, while accreditation standards guide the development and evaluation of health workforce education programs, identifying strengths and weaknesses to stimulate quality improvement. Continuing Professional Development (CPD): CPD encompasses training beyond clinical updates, including research, scientific writing, professionalism, communication, leadership, and team-building skills. CPD may be mandatory or voluntary, with verifiable activities documented to meet educational objectives. Health Workforce Education and Training: Health workforce education institutions provide accredited programs to train new health workers. These institutions may be public or private and are classified based on management rather than funding. Training programs aim to improve health knowledge, skills, and competencies, often with restricted enrollment (numerus clausus) to manage capacity. Health Workforce Planning: It includes addressing issues such as dropout rates, dual practice, and mobility of health professionals. Health Information Systems: These systems support decision-making by collecting, analyzing, and synthesizing data from health and other sectors. International Health Regulations (2005): This legal framework, binding on 196 countries, aims to prevent and respond to acute public health risks that cross borders, safeguarding global health security. Lifelong Learning: Lifelong learning encompasses all forms of education and training throughout life, enhancing knowledge, skills, and competencies. It includes formal, non-formal, and informal learning, supported by integrated systems such as schools, universities, and community-based facilities. This detailed categorization and explanation provide a comprehensive understanding of the health workforce, its education, and its operational frameworks.
